question: Can a frozen sender trace anonymous public wiring and learn which questions to switch together to shorten a physical packet while retaining all four delayed answers?
inputs: Four public questions with signed source occurrences. The sender alone sees the nine-bit state. Both endpoints know the fitted controller and the earlier frozen NAND parser.
forbidden_inputs: The delayed port at the sender, grader truth or optimal groups at inference, raw input or mask identifiers at the receiver, family/layout names, historical outcome labels or test-driven refits.
outputs: A physical binary tuple of wiring-dependent fixed length and an independently routed answer for the delayed port.
mapping: Fit public tracing and switch choices from training answers and packet width. Compare strict one-switch search, anonymous joint trials and a fitted single direct proposal.
primary_observable: Exact delayed answers on all 512 inputs and all four questions together with physical packet length and the independent number of answer vectors per wiring.
comparators_or_controls: Saved predecessor widths, raw-only and all-computed messages, exhaustive best raw/computed plan, strict singleton switching, held renaming and incidence changes, and a three-bit relation needing computation across answers.
resource_budget: One deterministic training-panel fit per declared strategy on 256 even-parity inputs. Four ports, at most 16 subsets of ports. Test every input including all odd-parity inputs. Use the shared CPU runner.
first_executable_signal: A physical packet from a frozen policy changes width between a dependent and independent delayed query set while preserving the truth of all ports.
stop_rule: Score the stored checkpoints once on the declared wirings. Preserve all high-width cases or decoder errors. No tuning against test outcomes.
nonclaims: Finite communication and task-transfer evidence. This study does not establish a speedup or an algorithm for arbitrary encoders or formula families.
